git commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
fix(io): `stream_get_wrappers()` listed `file`, and NOTHING honoured it

A fresh 30-program differential sweep of the streams surface turned up one
disagreement, and behind it a wrapper advertised but never implemented. MEASURED
against `php -n` 8.5.6 — twelve operations, one URL, every one of them false:

    file_get_contents  fopen  file_exists  filesize  is_file  file
    copy  file_put_contents  is_dir  mkdir  unlink  rename

php reads `file:///path` without complaint, and `stream_get_wrappers()` in elephc
already promised it would.

THE RULE, measured rather than reasoned about: `file://` matches case-insensitively
and needs exactly `://` — `file:/abs` and `file:abs` are filenames. What follows is
an authority then a path, and the authority must be EMPTY or exactly `localhost`,
also case-insensitively. `file://u.txt` is therefore a URL whose host is `u.txt`
and whose path is empty, which php refuses even with that file sitting right
there — the case a naive seven-byte strip opens while looking right everywhere
else. Extra slashes belong to the path: `file:////abs` opens `//abs`.

`__rt_path_cstr` is the front end to `__rt_cstr` that applies it, so the strip
lives in ONE place and every path builtin gets it by calling the front end instead.
The prefix is dropped by moving the pointer, never by copying.

NOT EVERY PATH BUILTIN takes it, and the split is not "is it a path" but "does php
call its plain-files wrapper or libc": `realpath()`, `readlink()`, the link
argument of `symlink()`, `glob()`, `disk_free_space()` and `chdir()` all answer
false for a `file://` URL in php. Each was measured; each keeps calling `__rt_cstr`
directly, and a test pins them so a later tidy-up cannot make them "uniform".

The strip touches only the scratch `__rt_cstr` already clobbers — that is why
`localhost` is compared against immediates rather than a data symbol, whose address
would need a register the callers still expect to survive. A unit test holds that
line on both architectures.

Known residual: a FAILING `file://` open names the resolved path in its warning
where php names the URL. php only does that for the stream-open family — `unlink`,
`rmdir`, `rename`, `touch` and `chmod` name the stripped path, which is already
what elephc prints. Left out here because the same probe found a larger
neighbouring gap: seven of those builtins emit NO warning at all on failure, and
`readfile()`/`file()` warn under the name `file_get_contents`.

Verified: the sweep is 30/30 identical, the 183-program round-8 corpus unchanged at
180, 1091 `io::` tests and 1535 unit tests pass. x86_64 mirrors the AArch64 arm
instruction for instruction; the CI x86 shard remains its execution oracle.
